package.name: busybox
package.description: swiss-army knife for embedded systems (Werewolf: applets exec applets by path)

trigger.script:
#!/usr/bin/busybox sh
for manifest in /etc/busybox-paths.d/*; do
  [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r path; do
    case "$path" in bin/sh|usr/bin/sh) continue ;; esac
    [ -e "/$path" ] || [ -L "/$path" ] || /usr/bin/busybox ln -s /usr/bin/busybox "/$path"
  done < "$manifest"
done

pipeline.name: Fetch the locked source commit
pipeline.runs:
git init -q .
for delay in 0 15 45; do
  sleep "$delay"
  for source in https://github.com/vda-linux/busybox_mirror.git https://git.busybox.net/busybox.git; do
    if git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c fetch.fsckObjects=true fetch --no-tags --depth=1 "$source" fc71374dfccd46448c62947269a35f1420d7ee28; then
      test "$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)" = fc71374dfccd46448c62947269a35f1420d7ee28
      git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout -q --detach fc71374dfccd46448c62947269a35f1420d7ee28
      exit 0
    fi
  done
done
echo "fc71374dfccd46448c62947269a35f1420d7ee28: every source failed, three times" >&2
exit 1

pipeline.name: Configure
pipeline.runs:
cp ../busyboxconfig .config
# Werewolf: an applet run by name runs from /usr/bin/busybox, with no PATH
# search, which Werewolf's glibc refuses (devel/busybox/README.md).
sed -i 's/^# CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS is not set$/CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS=y/' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS=y' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_BUSYBOX_EXEC_PATH="/usr/bin/busybox"' .config
make CC="${{host.triplet.gnu}}-gcc" V=1 -j$(nproc)

pipeline.name: Install
pipeline.runs:
mkdir -p "${{targets.destdir}}"/usr/bin
mkdir -p "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/busybox-paths.d
install -m755 busybox "${{targets.destdir}}"/usr/bin/busybox
install -m644 ../securetty "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/securetty
./busybox --list-path > "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/busybox-paths.d/busybox
# /bin/sh belongs to mksh, including developer images.
sed -i '\|^bin/sh$|d;\|^usr/bin/sh$|d' "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/busybox-paths.d/busybox

# sbin merge
sed 's|^sbin|usr/bin|' -i "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/busybox-paths.d/busybox
# bin merge
sed 's|^bin|usr/bin|' -i "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/busybox-paths.d/busybox
# usrsbin merge
sed 's|^usr/sbin|usr/bin|' -i "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/busybox-paths.d/busybox

pipeline.runs:
cp ../busyboxconfig-full .config
# Werewolf: an applet run by name runs from /usr/bin/busybox, with no PATH

pipeline.name: test that the busybox binary is dynamically linked
pipeline.runs:
if ! readelf -Wl /usr/bin/busybox | grep -E '^ *DYNAMIC +' ; then
  echo "FAIL: check to ensure busybox is dynamically linked failed"
  echo "The DYNAMIC field should exist in the ELF program header, output follows"
  readelf -Wl /usr/bin/busybox
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: busybox is dynamically linked"

pipeline.name: Verify network utilities are present
pipeline.runs:
busybox --help
busybox --list-full >full.txt
# These programs are expected to be present
for p in nc netcat wget nslookup; do
    if ! grep "usr/bin/$p" full.txt; then
        echo "$p is not present in busybox --list-full output"
        exit 1
    fi
    "$p" --help ||
      { echo "$p --help exited $?. expected pass"; exit 1; }
done

pipeline.name: Test wget can download a file
pipeline.runs:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
work=$(mktemp -d)
server=
trap 'test -z "$server" || kill "$server" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
printf '%s\n' 'wget test content' > "$work/expected"
# Serve one real HTTP response with BusyBox itself. No unrelated Python
# runtime or threaded server is needed to test the wget applet.
{
    printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' "$(wc -c < "$work/expected")"
    cat "$work/expected"
} | /usr/bin/busybox nc -l -p 8888 -w 10 > "$work/request" 2> "$work/server.log" &
server=$!
sleep 1
if ! /usr/bin/busybox wget -T 10 -O "$work/downloaded" http://127.0.0.1:8888/test.txt; then
    cat "$work/server.log"
    exit 1
fi
wait "$server"
server=
cmp "$work/expected" "$work/downloaded"
grep -F 'GET /test.txt ' "$work/request"
echo 'PASS: wget successfully downloaded the local HTTP response'

pipeline.name: Test nc can make network connections
pipeline.runs:
# Start nc listening in background, will send test data to first connection
echo "nc test data" | nc -l -p 9999 &
LISTEN_PID=$!

# Wait for listener to be ready
sleep 1

# Connect to the listening nc and capture data
result=$(nc 127.0.0.1 9999)

# Wait for listener to finish
wait "$LISTEN_PID"

# Verify data was transferred
if [ "$result" = "nc test data" ]; then
  echo "PASS: nc network connection works"
else
  echo "FAIL: nc did not receive expected data"
  echo "Expected: nc test data"
  echo "Got: $result"
  exit 1
fi

pipeline.name: Tools run applets by name without searching PATH
pipeline.runs:
cat > /tmp/busybox-probe.sh <<'WEREWOLF_BUSYBOX_PROBE'
# Each tool that runs a command runs an applet named bare from busybox itself:
# with PATH naming nothing, the PATH search a plain execvp would need finds no
# program, as Werewolf's glibc searches none.
set -eu
for tool in env 'timeout 5' nohup nice setsid flock\ /tmp/busybox-probe.lock; do
	# shellcheck disable=SC2086 # the tool's words split on purpose
	PATH=/nonexistent /usr/bin/busybox $tool true
done
echo x | PATH=/nonexistent /usr/bin/busybox xargs true
PATH=/nonexistent /usr/bin/busybox time true 2> /dev/null
rm -f /tmp/busybox-probe.lock

# All variants leave /bin/sh to the standalone shell package.
for manifest in /etc/busybox-paths.d/*; do
    [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue
    if /usr/bin/busybox grep -Eq '^(usr/)?bin/sh$' "$manifest"; then
        echo "BusyBox claims /bin/sh: $manifest" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done
WEREWOLF_BUSYBOX_PROBE
/usr/bin/busybox sh /tmp/busybox-probe.sh

pipeline.name: Configure
pipeline.runs:
sed -e 's/^# CONFIG_STATIC is not set$/CONFIG_STATIC=y/' \
    -e 's/^# CONFIG_STATIC_LIBGCC is not set/CONFIG_STATIC_LIBGCC=y/' \
    -e 's/^# CONFIG_USE_BB_PWD_GRP is not set/CONFIG_USE_BB_PWD_GRP=y/' \
    -e 's/^# CONFIG_USE_BB_SHADOW is not set/CONFIG_USE_BB_SHADOW=y/' \
    -e 's/^# CONFIG_USE_BB_CRYPT is not set/CONFIG_USE_BB_CRYPT=y/' \
    -e 's/^# CONFIG_USE_BB_CRYPT_SHA is not set/CONFIG_USE_BB_CRYPT_SHA=y/' \
    ../busyboxconfig > .config
# yescrypt (USE_BB_CRYPT_YES, new in 1.38.0) is a sub-option of
# USE_BB_CRYPT, which is disabled in the base config, so there is no
# line to substitute above; append it
echo "CONFIG_USE_BB_CRYPT_YES=y" >> .config
# emit diff for verification, diff returns 1 on differences,
# ensure there actually is a difference
rc=0
diff -u ../busyboxconfig .config || rc="$?"
if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
   echo "ERROR: expected the generated static config to differ from the default config" >&2
   exit 1
fi
# Werewolf: an applet run by name runs from /usr/bin/busybox, with no PATH
# search, which Werewolf's glibc refuses (devel/busybox/README.md).
sed -i 's/^# CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS is not set$/CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS=y/' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS=y' .config
grep -qx 'CONFIG_BUSYBOX_EXEC_PATH="/usr/bin/busybox"' .config
make CC="${{host.triplet.gnu}}-gcc" V=1 -j$(nproc)

pipeline.name: awk = and ?: precedence
pipeline.runs:
found=$(awk 'BEGIN { a=0?"bug":"ok"; print a}')
[ "$found" = "ok" ] &&
  echo "PASS: ternary precedence" ||

pipeline.name: test that busybox is built not to use nsswitch.conf functionality
pipeline.runs:
# if busybox is statically linked against glibc and is not
# built to use its own passwd/shadow reading functions,
# functions will fail if /etc/nsswitch.conf is present but
# the libnsswitch_* libraries are not; e.g.:
#   $ whoami
#   whoami: unknown uid 65532
# Confirm this by setting up a chroot with the necessary
# files and nsswitch.conf and that whoami still works as
# expected.
mkdir -p /tmp/whoami/bin
cp /usr/bin/busybox /tmp/whoami/bin/whoami
mkdir -p /tmp/whoami/etc
cp /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/group /etc/nsswitch.conf /tmp/whoami/etc
chroot /tmp/whoami/ /bin/whoami | grep '^root$' &&
  echo "PASS: whoami works in presence of nsswitch.conf" ||
  { echo "FAIL: whoami failed to lookup username with nsswitch.conf" ;
    echo "This likely means busybox is using glibc's libnss" ;
    echo "Verify busybox is built with CONFIG_USE_BB_PWD_GRP" ;
    exit 1;
  }
